note: Gratus Grace's lines. Plain, under twelve words, sage-like: says less, sees more, never flatters, never scolds. Never the same line twice to the same person. Every line here is flagged for the owner (owner: true on the file).

none: What is here, right now, that you almost walked past?
Name one small thing that worked today.
Something ordinary carried you today. Which?
joy: Where did the light come from today?
What made you laugh, and who was there?
Notice the thing you want to keep.
calm: What is quiet in you right now?
Which slow thing did you let be slow?
Name what needed nothing from you today.
love: Who was easy to be near today?
What did you give without being asked?
Notice the hand that was there.
hope: What is leaning toward morning in you?
Which small thing pointed somewhere good?
What are you quietly counting on?
sad: What is heavy, and where are you holding it?
One small thing was still good. Which?
What did you manage, even so?
afraid: What is the fear standing in front of?
Notice one thing that stayed steady.
What would you see if you looked at it?
angry: What did the anger want to protect?
Where is the heat in you now?
Name the line that was crossed.
tired: What can rest tonight without your help?
One thing was enough today. Which?
Notice what your body already did.

none: Where does today sit in your body?
Feel first. Then find the word.
joy: Name the joy before it slips off.
Where in you did the good land?
calm: Calm has a texture. Describe it.
Where does the quiet live in you?
Name what let you set it down.
love: Love has a place in the body. Find it.
What does the warmth feel like, exactly?
hope: Name the thing you are hoping toward.
Where does hope sit: chest, hands, throat?
Say the wish out loud, in ink.
sad: Say the sad thing in one sentence.
Where does it ache? Start there.
Naming it does not make it larger.
afraid: Name the fear in a sentence. Just that.
Where is the tightness? Breathe into it.
Fear gets smaller when it has a name.
angry: Name the anger without arguing with it.
Where is it: jaw, fists, chest?
What is underneath it? Name that too.
tired: Where does the weight sit tonight?
Tired is a feeling. Name it, then rest.

none: Pick up yesterday's thread. Add one line.
What do you want more of tomorrow?
Which plant could use a day from you?
joy: Keep this. Write it down before sleep.
What made the joy possible? Tend that.
Return to a good thing on purpose.
calm: A week of calm. What is holding it?
Set one intention for tomorrow morning.
Keep the practice that keeps you.
love: Who made today easier? Say their name.
Tend the person, not just the feeling.
What would you do again tomorrow?
hope: When this happens tomorrow, I will…
Tend the small thing pointing somewhere.
What is the next step, plainly?
sad: A small kindness for tomorrow. Name it.
What helped, even a little? Keep it.
afraid: Who could stand beside you in this?
Name one steady thing to return to.
What is the smallest next step?
angry: What did this teach? One line.
Write the letter you will not send.
Tend the boundary, not the fire.
tired: Tend one thing. Leave the rest.
One word from the body, then sleep.

none: Who deserves a thank you today?
A note to future you. Where to start?
What would you give if you could?
joy: Joy gives itself away. To whom?
Who needs to hear this today?
calm: Give a little of the quiet away.
Write to someone who is not calm.
Whose morning could you make easier?
love: Write to them. Send it or not.
What would you want them to know?
Give the words you keep meaning to say.
hope: Write a note to your future self.
Give someone the thing you are hoping for.
Who could carry this hope with you?
sad: A letter to what was lost.
Who else is carrying something today?
Give yourself the kindness you would give a friend.
afraid: Tell one person what frightens you.
Give the fear a smaller job.
Who would you want beside you?
angry: What do you want to protect? Give that.
A letter, unsent, to the one who crossed the line.
Turn the heat toward something you can build.
tired: Give yourself tomorrow off from one thing.
Who could you ask for help?
Rest is a gift. Accept it.

none: What do you keep coming back to?
Pick one thread from this week. Pull it.
What is still true from a month ago?
joy: Which joy is worth returning to tomorrow?
Go back to the good moment. Add a detail.
What made today's light? Keep the recipe.
calm: What practice is holding the calm?
Return to yesterday's quiet. Is it still here?
Name the habit you want to keep.
love: Who do you keep returning to?
Write the next line of a long thank-you.
What would you do again, on purpose?
hope: What are you still hoping toward?
Return to the plan. What is the next step?
sad: What helped last time? Return to it.
Pick up the thread gently. One line.
What has stayed steady through this?
afraid: What steadied you before? Go there again.
Return to the plainest next step.
Who has stood beside you before?
angry: What did you decide last time this rose?
Return to the line you drew.
tired: What restored you before? Return to it.
One line, then the bed that knows you.
Which small thing can wait until morning?

program.title: Grow With Gratus
lines: Grow With Gratus is the program behind the garden: you write, you plant, you tend; the garden pays you in $GRATUS for showing up; the fruit you grow can be given, and every gift carries the days it took.

Grow Together: a Gratus Group is a shared plot for two or more people — a couple, a family, a team, a classroom, a memorial. A plant becomes Common Ground only when two people plant the same thing and both accept it.
Gratus Give: causes with public gardens anyone can plant into. Verified causes pay no fee. Community projects are marked plainly.
Nothing here has levels, ranks, or leaderboards. Everyone is equal on this ground.
